statement: The Bash tool's cwd silently pointed at a stale sibling checkout (C:/Projects/enforcer-rust, a different repo location pinned at commit 11:42 before my lib.rs edits) rather than my assigned worktree (C:/Projects/ocentra-enforcer/.claude/worktrees/agent-abdf04ee1cd5c751f). `cargo test -p enforcer-plan` ran there, found 0 tests, and gave no error -- it silently compiled a stale lib.rs missing `pub mod validator;` instead of failing.
why: A worker's Bash/PowerShell tool cwd is not guaranteed to start in (or stay pinned to) the git worktree named in the dispatch prompt; there can be an unrelated same-named-crate checkout elsewhere on disk that silently absorbs commands with plausible-looking (but wrong) output. Zero tests found is easy to misread as 'my test module didn't get compiled in' rather than 'this isn't even my worktree'.
howToApply: Before trusting a `cargo test`/`cargo build` result during a worker session, run `pwd` (or `git status --short`) and confirm the path matches the worktree path given in the dispatch prompt AND that `git status` shows your own uncommitted edits. A 0-tests-found or suspiciously-fast build is a strong signal to re-verify cwd before debugging the code.

evidence.ref: cargo test -p enforcer-plan returned 0 tests from /c/Projects/enforcer-rust while edits lived in the ocentra-enforcer worktree

statement: Running the b02 PLAN-CAPSULE/PLAN-SKELETON/PLAN-FRONTMATTER validators against this repo's own live docs/plans/enforcer-selfhost-plan/workpacks/ (113 files) found 95 real findings: most workpacks predate the current agent-capsule wording (older 'Read when: Only when this exact workpack is assigned.' vs current '... or selected from WORKPACK_INDEX.md.') and many `tier:` lines use free-form English tokens (unit/CI/install-proof/contract/schema, or dual P-tokens like P1/P5) instead of the strict `P0-P5 [T1-T3]` grammar this workpack's own text implies is canon.
why: This plan's own PLAN_STATE.md already records 'No workpack is DONE' -- the 113 workpacks were authored progressively and the capsule/tier grammar tightened partway through, so drift across older vs newer docs is real and expected, not a validator bug. A hard-fail self-host test asserting zero findings across all 113 sibling docs would make b02 responsible for silently blocking on -- or worse, being pressured to edit -- 111 files it does not own.
howToApply: Split the self-host proof into two tiers: (1) a strict zero-findings assertion scoped ONLY to the one workpack file this pack fully owns/controls (its own b02-*.md), which genuinely gates cargo test; (2) a separate bonus-proof test that runs the same validators read-only across the full live plan dir, asserts the scan itself is non-hollow (ran > 0 files), and persists the finding count/detail to the named proof artifact path (proof/plan/b02-selfhost.txt) instead of gating on it. Report the aggregate finding count to the dispatcher as selfPlanFindings rather than silently fixing sibling docs.

evidence.ref: proof/plan/b02-selfhost.txt: scanned 113 live workpacks, found 95 PLAN-* findings

statement: enforcer-rules ships two shapes of rule record: JSON catalogs under `rules/*.json` (baseline T1 deny-wall/no-reexports/posture records, loaded via include_str! + parse_catalog) and, new with b02, a typed Rust constructor module under `src/rules/<family>.rs` (here `plan.rs`, exposing `plan_rule_records() -> Result<Vec<RuleRecord>, RuleLoadError>`). The typed-Rust shape is worth choosing over JSON specifically when a rule family's ValidatorRef.path literals are meant to compile-check against a sibling crate's real module paths during THIS crate's own test run (a JSON string can silently drift from the validator it names; a Rust &str constant re-used by both crates' test modules cannot drift without a compile-checked rename).
why: ValidatorRef deliberately stores crate_name/path as free strings (enforcer-rules does not depend on enforcer-plan, to avoid a cycle), so nothing mechanically forces the string to match a real symbol. Shipping the record constructor as Rust lets that crate's own parity test (every_plan_record_fixture_path_exists_on_disk) assert the fixture paths resolve on disk, and keeps the RuleId literals as named constants that a future rename in enforcer-plan's validator module would need a matching intentional edit here, not just a JSON edit nobody re-validates.
howToApply: When adding a new rule family whose ValidatorRef will point at symbols in a crate enforcer-rules cannot depend on, default to the JSON-catalog shape UNLESS the family's authors want the tighter coupling: then ship `src/rules/<family>.rs` with a `pub fn <family>_rule_records() -> Result<Vec<RuleRecord>, RuleLoadError>` and a same-module parity test that walks the workspace root and asserts every fixtures.fail/fixtures.pass path exists on disk.
